content:
The image shows the underside of a soybean leaf with small, discrete tan-to-reddish-brown spots scattered across the surface. Key observations:

- **Location**: Underside of leaf (abaxial surface)
- **Lesion color**: Small tan/orange-brown to brick-red spots
- **Lesion shape**: Small, round to irregular pustule-like spots
- **Distribution**: Scattered across the leaf, not coalescing
- **Leaf tissue**: Otherwise green and healthy-looking between spots
- **No angular shape** (rules out bacterial blight)
- **No gray centers with red borders** (rules out frogeye)
- **No large brown blotches** (rules out septoria brown spot at advanced stage)

The small tan-to-brick-red spots on the **underside** of the leaf are highly characteristic of **soybean rust** — which produces urediniospore-containing pustules on the lower leaf surface. The coloring (tan/orange-brown to red-brown) and the discrete, small, scattered nature of these lesions on the abaxial surface match the rust description precisely.
